matching_proof.method: For each non-timing stop use its adjacent route timing points to define eligible arrivals for each trip. The sorted chronological join provides a complete bipartite matching. Remove each matched edge individually and recompute maximum matching; if every removal reduces size by one, no alternative complete matching exists. This is checked independently at all50 non-timing stops.
assumptions: Each per-stop published arrival is one occurrence of one route trip in the same explicit service and direction.
A trip serves its indicated origin-to-terminus common stop suffix; the current route timetable trip-specific timing-point sequences and observed stop-schedule counts verify the two suffix patterns.
Intermediate scheduled arrivals occur between adjacent published timing-point arrivals.

limits: Per-stop responses omit trip_id; intermediate identity is uniquely derived under the documented complete-timetable constraints.
Only six stops are designated timing points. Other stop times are operator-published scheduled references whose interpolation algorithm is undocumented.
This does not establish actual morning running times, bus dwell, traffic signals, tailgating, queue spillback, vehicle blocks, driver duties, recovery time or vehicle reuse across trips.
A timetable service layer across the full line is distinct from calibrated microscopic road simulation; the current native street extent is Porto.
The API service_days flags are all false/null despite date-resolved active service; the explicit services?date=2026-10-28 response is the date authority.
